This gallery is for evidence from real classroom and shop projects—not only polished outcomes. Each case study should make the cycle visible:

<div class="ter-process-flow ter-process-flow--strong" aria-label="Organizer design cycle"><span>DESIGN</span><span>BUILD</span><span>FEEDBACK</span><span>REVISION</span></div>

## What every gallery entry should include

Finished photo; original sketch/drawing; problem; key dimensions; materials; fabrication method; what worked; feedback; next revision; source/downloads where appropriate; and a clear validation status. If evidence is missing, say so instead of filling the gap with a stock or generated image.

## TIJ1OR-E Knife Holder Design

::: {.ter-case-status}
**Revision 2 · March 22, 2024**

**Drawing available · finished-project photo pending**

The source drawing is described in the project record but is not yet available in a publishable local/connected file. No substitute image has been invented. Add the actual drawing and classroom photo here after source permission and student privacy are confirmed.
:::

<div class="ter-case-study-grid">
<section>

### Problem and design strengths

The design creates freestanding storage for knives/tools using individual, visible positions. It supports quick visual counting, easy access and simple wood construction. Its orthographic and isometric views are useful examples of communicating a fabrication idea.

### Drawing facts

- drawing title: **TIJ1OR-E Knife Holder Design**;
- units: inches;
- identified materials: wood, screws and rope;
- projecting supports/nails: approximately **2 in spacing**;
- projecting length: approximately **2 in**;
- insertion: approximately **1/2 in**;
- angle: approximately **35°**.

</section>
<section>

### Feedback / next revision brief

Investigate a revision that:

- can hang on a wall, preferably with removable mounting;
- can work on both a wall and a bench;
- avoids back-to-back attachment storage;
- keeps one clearly accessible working face;
- preserves visibility and one-handed removal;
- considers a French cleat or another removable interface.

These are design-review notes, not a complete redesign. The useful strengths of Revision 2 should remain visible in the next concept.

</section>
</div>

## Reference systems and tools

The [pill-bottle organizer assembly gallery](../../03-laser-cutting/resources/pill-bottle-organizer.qmd) contains five labelled **reference systems** with exploded views and downloads; they are not presented as physically verified student builds. Use the [Fabrication Plate Builder](../plate-builder/index.qmd), [laser SVG library](../../../teaching-materials/laser-cutting/index.qmd), [calibration workflow](../../03-laser-cutting/04-material-fit-calibration.qmd), palettes and component files as starting infrastructure—then measure, test and document the actual build.

## Add a future build

Use the same evidence fields above. Do not mark a design “validated” merely because a file renders or a digital assembly looks plausible. Distinguish **drawing available**, **dimension-tested**, **fit-tested**, **shop-tested**, and **photo documented**.
